b2f2f98188a5.exp: The clove hitch (ballestrinque) is the knot for tying a rope to a fixed cylindrical object such as a handrail, stanchion (candelero) or post: it is made with two turns and is firm, although it admits tension in one direction only. The bowline (as de guía) forms a bight (seno), the reef knot (nudo llano) joins ropes of equal thickness and the round turn and two half hitches (vuelta de rezón) is for rings or anchors.

e4ef0de7ce59.exp: The clove hitch (ballestrinque) is the knot for tying a rope to a fixed cylindrical object such as a handrail, stanchion (candelero) or post: it is made with two turns and is firm, although it admits tension in one direction only. The bowline (as de guía) forms a bight (seno), the reef knot (nudo llano) joins ropes of equal thickness and the round turn and two half hitches (vuelta de rezón) is for rings or anchors.

8c2269f24185.exp: The sounder measures the depth below the transducer; the equipment is usually calibrated (offset) to give the distance between the keel and the bottom, that is, the water available under the boat. It does not give the height of the tide nor the draught (calado), which is the submerged part of the hull. This helps avoid running aground (varar).
8c2269f24185.duda: The typical sounder shows the depth from the transducer (adjustable), not necessarily the distance between keel and bottom; option b is ambiguous.

4e98123cfc31.exp: The end (chicote) is the free end of a rope or cable. The standing part (firme) is the fixed or secured end, the bight (seno) is the curved or slack part between the two ends and the mooring line (boza) is a short rope used for tying up or securing. Rule: chicote = free tip; firme = the side that is tied.

e61028007d18.exp: The end (chicote) is the free end of a rope or cable. The standing part (firme) is the fixed or secured end, the bight (seno) is the curved or slack part between the two ends and the mooring line (boza) is a short rope used for tying up or securing. Rule: chicote = free tip; firme = the side that is tied.

8d7a961af734.exp: Bitts (bitas) are solid cylindrical pieces, fixed to the deck, used to make fast mooring lines. Mooring posts (noráis) are on the quay, stanchions (candeleros) hold the handrails or lifelines (guardamancebos) and the bollard (bolardo) is the equivalent piece on the quay. Note: bita = on the boat.

8119e2223af9.exp: Mooring lines are made fast on the bitts (bitas), fixed deck pieces. Bollards (bolardos) and mooring posts (noráis) are found on the quay, stanchions (candeleros) hold the lifelines (guardamancebos) or handrails and the fairleads (guías) only direct the rope. Memorise: bita on the boat, norai on the quay.

151c67312fc0.exp: The buoy rope (orinque) is the rope, attached to the anchor ring (arganeo) or the crown (cruz) of the anchor at one end and to a small buoy (boyarín) at the other, which marks the position of the anchor and lets you free it if it gets fouled on rocks. The anchor is buoyed (se orinca) on rocky bottoms or with obstacles, where it could get trapped. Mnemonic: orinque = anchor 'on a leash'.

657452695a5d.exp: The buoy rope (orinque) is the rope, attached to the anchor ring (arganeo) or the crown (cruz) of the anchor at one end and to a small buoy (boyarín) at the other, which marks the position of the anchor and lets you free it if it gets fouled on rocks. The anchor is buoyed (se orinca) on rocky bottoms or with obstacles, where it could get trapped. Mnemonic: orinque = anchor 'on a leash'.

539f1c6b89b3.exp: The buoy rope (orinque) is the rope or chain attached at one end to the anchor and at the other to a small buoy (boyarín), marking its position. The link (malla) is a chain link, the anchor ring (arganeo) is the ring of the anchor and the bitter end/anchor fastening (arraigado) is the point where the chain is secured at the bottom of the chain locker. Memorise: orinque = anchor marker.

fe0d94905341.exp: Rope guides (guía cabos) are pieces, fixed to the hull, that direct the mooring lines from the boat to the mooring post (noray) or bitt of the quay, avoiding chafing and wear. They do not hold the anchor chain, nor the halyard, nor the boat hook.

be470b115717.exp: Taking bearings or references of notable points on land (and checking that they do not change) lets you quickly detect whether the anchor is dragging (garrea), because the boat's position relative to them varies. It is not for finding out the latitude, the depth or whether one could swim ashore.

a59795eceeab.exp: Taking bearings or references of notable points on land (and checking that they do not change) lets you quickly detect whether the anchor is dragging (garrea), because the boat's position relative to them varies. It is not for finding out the latitude, the depth or whether one could swim ashore.

f8a1073e79a4.exp: Taking bearings or references of notable points on land (and checking that they do not change) lets you quickly detect whether the anchor is dragging (garrea), because the boat's position relative to them varies. It is not for finding out the latitude, the depth or whether one could swim ashore.

b486f895904a.exp: The bowline (as de guía) forms a fixed eye (gaza, bight) that does not slip at the end of a rope, useful as a temporary mooring loop or to rescue someone. It is not a harness nor is it used to shorten a rope (for that there are the sheepshank (margarita) or the clove hitch (ballestrinque)). It is a secure knot and easy to undo.

b26ab747d002.exp: On rocky bottoms the anchor can wedge between rocks and not come free. To avoid it, it is buoyed (orinca): a rope (orinque) is tied to the anchor ring (arganeo) or crown (cruz) of the anchor and marked with a small buoy (boyarín), so you can pull from above on the orinque and release it backwards. Paying out more chain or anchoring from the stern does not prevent fouling (enrocamiento).

c45d78c89750.exp: Buoying the anchor (orincar) is advisable when there is a risk of it getting fouled or trapped on the bottom (rocks, wrecks, chains): the buoy rope (orinque) lets you haul it up from the other side. It does not serve to prevent dragging (garreo) or swinging (borneo), nor does it depend on anchoring to leeward.

60f5a3de2417.exp: Buoying the anchor (orincar) is advisable when there is a risk of it getting fouled or trapped on the bottom (rocks, wrecks, chains): the buoy rope (orinque) lets you haul it up from the other side. It does not serve to prevent dragging (garreo) or swinging (borneo), nor does it depend on anchoring to leeward.

0a0012da371e.exp: If the anchor drags (garrea), the first thing is to try to make it hold by paying out (filando) more chain, which increases the holding force and the favourable pull angle. If that does not work, weigh anchor and anchor again. Signals and calls to Salvamento are later measures, if the dragging cannot be controlled.

d0b10997b84c.exp: In good weather, the length of chain paid out should be at least about three times the depth (sonda); in bad weather it is increased (five or more). With less length the pull would be almost vertical and the anchor would drag. 10 to 13 times would be excessive and does not fit in most anchorages.

66dacb7cf8cb.exp: Berthing bow-to or stern-to (atracar de punta) means placing the boat perpendicular to the quay, with the bow or the stern towards it (held by lateral lines and the anchor or mooring block on the opposite side). Berthing alongside (de costado), on the other hand, is going alongside with port or starboard to the quay. It does not depend on the wind.

62184a74cb53.exp: Berthing bow-to or stern-to (atracar de punta) means placing the boat perpendicular to the quay, with the bow or the stern towards it (held by lateral lines and the anchor or mooring block on the opposite side). Berthing alongside (de costado), on the other hand, is going alongside with port or starboard to the quay. It does not depend on the wind.

83457f68d4b2.exp: The drawing shows a bowline (as de guía): a knot that forms a fixed bight that does not slip and is easily undone even under tension. It is recognised because the end (chicote) comes out inside the eye (gaza), going round the standing part (firme) (the rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree and goes back into the hole). The clove hitch (ballestrinque) is two crossed turns and the round turn and two half hitches (vuelta de rezón) is two hitches (cotes).

b8eb60e69c7d.exp: The knot in the drawing is a clove hitch (ballestrinque): two turns on a cylindrical object, with the second crossing over the first and the end tucked under it. It serves for tying to a handrail or post, but must have tension in one direction only. The bowline (as de guía) forms a bight (seno) and the reef knot (nudo llano) joins two ropes.

dde181657a42.exp: The sheave (roldana) is the rotating piece, at the end of the bow, over which the anchor line slides, reducing chafing. The buoy rope (orinque) marks the position of the anchor, the swinging circle (círculo de borneo) is the turning area of the anchored boat and the steering wheel governs the course.

d126bb1f3f70.exp: The mooring block (muerto) is a large weight, generally of reinforced concrete, placed on the bottom, to which a chain or rope with a buoy is shackled for mooring boats. The mooring post (noray) and the bollard (bolardo) are on the quay, and the floor timber (varenga) is a structural piece of the hull.

8316df85c255.exp: The utensil in the drawing is a boat hook (bichero), a pole with a hook at the tip used to reach or pull in ropes, buoys and other objects, or to fend the boat off when berthing. The rope guide (guía cabos) and the cleat (cornamusa) are fixed deck pieces and the claw (garra) is part of the grapnel anchor (rezón).

f4b6c04ffbe0.exp: The cleat (cornamusa) is the two-armed metal piece fixed to the deck used to make fast mooring lines (they are made fast with turns and a locking hitch (vuelta falsa)). It is not a support for flags, antennas or fishing rods.

58b270dbf932.exp: The ventilation cowl (manguerote) is a ventilation duct on deck, with the mouth that can be turned into the wind, which allows the air in the interior compartments to be renewed while preventing water from entering. Closing the compartment to prevent water entering is not its function, but it does not serve for lighting either.

442bcf2c4eca.exp: The round turn and two half hitches (vuelta de rezón) is the suitable knot for joining the anchor line (rope or chain) to the anchor ring (arganeo): two hitches and a turn that withstands a lot of tension and is easily undone, although it is usually secured with a seizing (barbiquejo). The clove hitch (ballestrinque) and the reef knot (llano) are not recommended here and the bowline (as de guía) can come loose by chafing.

09550ddda443.exp: The round turn and two half hitches (vuelta de rezón) is the suitable knot for joining the anchor line (rope or chain) to the anchor ring (arganeo): two hitches and a turn that withstands a lot of tension and is easily undone, although it is usually secured with a seizing (barbiquejo). The clove hitch (ballestrinque) and the reef knot (llano) are not recommended here and the bowline (as de guía) can come loose by chafing.

80ba70e68469.exp: Soft mud is the worst holding ground (tenedero): the anchor penetrates but offers hardly any resistance and drags easily. Hard mud, clay and gravel (cascajo) offer better holding. The best bottoms are sand and firm mud.

50d60bc2a205.exp: The sheave (roldana) is the rotating piece installed at the bow end, over which the anchor line slides and which reduces friction. The rigid piece for making fast lines is the bitt (bita) or cleat (cornamusa), the fender (defensa) protects against knocks and the machine for weighing anchor is the windlass (molinete) or capstan (cabrestante).

65aa17214415.exp: A suitable holding ground (tenedero) is a bottom of sand or mud where the anchor holds well and damage to the protected seagrass meadows (fanerógamas, posidonia) is avoided. On rock the anchor gets fouled and there is no secure hold. The tenedero is the bottom, not a place on board.

e29caad6576b.exp: A suitable holding ground (tenedero) is a bottom of sand or mud where the anchor holds well and damage to the protected seagrass meadows (fanerógamas, posidonia) is avoided. On rock the anchor gets fouled and there is no secure hold. The tenedero is the bottom, not a place on board.

2cb1f9a181bf.exp: When mooring to a buoy in a current, you head into the current, as when anchoring: the boat stays with its bow against the water, is more stable and the manoeuvre is more controllable. Putting the stern or the beam to the current would force mooring with the current pushing and the boat would drift (abatir) onto the buoy.

2240fbc65b72.exp: The hydrostatic release (zafa hidrostática) is the device that automatically releases the liferaft when the boat sinks, on reaching a certain water pressure (about 2-4 m). It cuts the lashing and lets the raft float; the painter (cabo disparador), attached to the hull, then makes it inflate. Mnemonic: hidro = water that triggers it.

44f94de8e011.exp: Portable extinguishers are placed in places of easy access and in view, so they can be used quickly if a fire breaks out. They are not placed near sources of fire, nor in the engine compartment nor shut away, because they would be disabled by the fire itself or inaccessible.

093c482cc2b8.exp: To reduce rolling (balances) you must change course and vary the angle at which the waves reach the boat: this avoids having the sea on the beam, which is what causes the most rolling. Increasing speed or moving weights can worsen stability; throwing weights overboard is unnecessary.

5765c29073e1.exp: Flares and rockets are fired to leeward (sotavento, the side the wind does not come from), so that the wind carries away the incandescent residues and they do not fall on the boat or the crew. The rocket is held with the arm extended and away from the body.

a5b91027f1af.exp: When someone falls over one side, the helm is put to that same side: the stern swings away from the person in the water and the propeller does not reach them. You must shout 'man overboard', throw the lifebuoy and not lose sight of the person. Putting the helm to the opposite side would bring the stern and the propeller towards the person in the water.

98f1c85dfc92.exp: When someone falls over one side, the helm is put to that same side: the stern swings away from the person in the water and the propeller does not reach them. You must shout 'man overboard', throw the lifebuoy and not lose sight of the person. Putting the helm to the opposite side would bring the stern and the propeller towards the person in the water.

72ed4f20754f.exp: When someone falls over one side, the helm is put to that same side: the stern swings away from the person in the water and the propeller does not reach them. You must shout 'man overboard', throw the lifebuoy and not lose sight of the person. Putting the helm to the opposite side would bring the stern and the propeller towards the person in the water.

95cbf9704f82.exp: When someone falls over one side, the helm is put to that same side: the stern swings away from the person in the water and the propeller does not reach them. You must shout 'man overboard', throw the lifebuoy and not lose sight of the person. Putting the helm to the opposite side would bring the stern and the propeller towards the person in the water.

083e1ee0d3ff.exp: The drawing shows a sector search (exploración por sectores): after the datum you sail tracing a pattern of triangles with turns of 120 degrees, like a star or a wheel with sectors. It is used when the position of the person in the water is known but they cannot be seen. The expanding square (espiral cuadrada) moves away from the datum on each turn and Boutakow is used with the person in the water in sight.

c4004e7da9af.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras) are dangerous because the boat can run aground (embarrancar), that is, ground or touch bottom (varar). They do not necessarily imply poor visibility, traffic or currents. You must consult the chart, watch the sounder and keep a safety margin.

b1bab97172c7.exp: The expanding square search (exploración en espiral cuadrada) consists of sailing around the datum moving away from it on each turn by a given distance, tracing a spiral with straight sides. It is used when the person in the water cannot be seen but the area is known. The circular search is just a circle around and Boutakow is used with the person in the water in sight.

d59eae1665ad.exp: When the person in the water can no longer be seen, they are searched for from the datum with an expanding square search (espiral cuadrada), which covers more and more area. Boutakow and Anderson are used with the person in the water in sight, and the circular one does not widen the area.
d59eae1665ad.duda: There is another identical question with the key 'sector search'; both methods are used when the person in the water cannot be seen, so the key is ambiguous.

4a3ed529a0c2.exp: The sector search (exploración por sectores) is a search manoeuvre for when the person in the water cannot be seen, starting from the known position (datum): tracks are run in sectors of 120 degrees. Boutakow and Anderson are for a person in the water in sight and the circular one is not the most suitable.
4a3ed529a0c2.duda: There is another identical question with the key 'expanding square'; both methods are used without seeing the person in the water, so the key is ambiguous.

dcbaabbbff45.exp: The manoeuvre in the drawing is the Anderson: the helm is put to the side of the fall until we have separated, then the boat is turned so that it returns over its wake and approaches the person in the water with the wind, stopping next to them. Williamson and Scharnow are turns to return to the wake with different angles, and Boutakow is a different curve.

e7a72dfb23bf.exp: The person in the water is picked up on the leeward side (sotavento): the boat is to windward of the person and shelters them from wind and waves, preventing them from being swept against the hull. To windward the drift of the boat would carry it onto the person in the water.

12690dade631.exp: The telephone number of Salvamento Marítimo for maritime emergencies is 900 202 202. You can also call 112 or make contact by VHF on channel 16. This number must be memorised, as it is the only one that corresponds to the Sociedad Estatal.

4eaca69929cb.exp: MOB is the GPS 'Man Overboard' function (hombre al agua): it immediately marks the position where the fall occurred and guides to it. MAN, GOTO and WAYPOINT are not emergency functions: GOTO and WAYPOINT are for navigating to points and MAN does not exist as such.

09640b4681f4.exp: Hypothermia (hipotermia) is a drop in body temperature below normal (about 37 C), common in castaways because of the cold water. Hyperthermia (hipertermia) is the opposite (an increase) and fainting (lipotimia) is a brief loss of consciousness. The prefix hipo- means 'below'.

928916204776.exp: Hypothermia (hipotermia) is a drop in body temperature below normal (about 37 C), common in castaways because of the cold water. Hyperthermia (hipertermia) is the opposite (an increase) and fainting (lipotimia) is a brief loss of consciousness. The prefix hipo- means 'below'.

5a4e55838bc9.exp: The towed boat puts its helm to the side opposite to the one the tug turns to. This way its bow follows the wake without approaching the line and avoids the 'estrechonazo' (a sudden jerk or collision against the tug). This compensates for the fact that the towed boat tends to go towards the inside of the curve.

7dbdee850a80.exp: Before sailing, among other things, the fuel level must be checked, so as not to run out at sea. The water temperature is not monitored, the seacocks must be open if cooling with sea water, and the oil is checked by level, not by temperature, before starting.

054f87eebb85.exp: Putting everything 'a son de mar' means leaving each thing stowed, secured and lashed so that nothing shifts or bangs with rolling or bad weather. It is a precaution before sailing, not a course or mooring manoeuvre.

ac12680a5a91.exp: Putting everything 'a son de mar' means leaving each thing stowed, secured and lashed so that nothing shifts or bangs with rolling or bad weather. It is a precaution before sailing, not a course or mooring manoeuvre.

edef74be08ce.exp: Stability (estabilidad) is the property of the boat of recovering its equilibrium position when an external cause (waves, wind, weights) makes it lose it. Buoyancy (flotabilidad) is the ability to float, seaworthiness (navegabilidad) is the fitness to sail safely and speed is just the advance per unit of time.

5c69d22e411a.exp: Stability (estabilidad) is the tendency of the boat to avoid a change of position or to recover the one lost due to an external disturbance. Buoyancy (flotabilidad) is staying afloat, seaworthiness (navegabilidad) is the fitness to sail and watertightness (estanqueidad) is not letting water through.

2843bdd34123.exp: The mandatory lifebuoy must carry an automatically activated light and a floating line (rabiza), so that it can be seen at night and the person in the water can be recovered. The SART radar transponder is different distress equipment and the buoy is not sufficient on its own.

ab6c4ccb45a4.exp: Stability improves by lowering the centre of gravity: weights are moved towards the keel, which increases the righting moment (momento de adrizamiento). Raising them to the deck lifts it and reduces stability, and shifting them to one side causes heel; moving them forward affects the trim (asiento), not the transverse stability.

ce2bbf5f6b67.exp: The raft must be stowed so as not to prevent its automatic floating free: without fixed lashings that hold it when the boat sinks, and with the hydrostatic release (zafa hidrostática) free. If it were enclosed or heavily lashed it would not be released. The lashing is not reinforced in bad weather, nor does it go in lockers (cofres).

28a9abed2d4e.exp: It is mandatory to carry one lifejacket for each person on board and, for children, one suited to their size for each child embarked. Carrying adult lifejackets is not enough, as they do not fit a child; nor is an extra 10% needed nor always two.

71b2894a1120.exp: The signalling mirror (espejo de señales) is also called a heliograph (heliógrafo): it reflects sunlight to attract attention and ask for help, visible at a great distance. The heliometer is an astronomical instrument, the radar reflector returns waves and the alidade is used to take relative bearings and bearings.

7a13f84cd119.exp: The signalling mirror (heliógrafo) uses reflected sunlight to ask for help and attract attention. The heliometer is an astronomical instrument, the radar reflector is passive and does not use sunlight, and the alidade is used to take relative bearings.

1e6f848e804a.exp: The water-settling filter (filtro de decantación, water separator) removes the impurities and the water the fuel contains before it reaches the injection pumps, and must be checked before leaving. The oil separator (separador oleico) treats bilge water, the sea strainer (filtro de fondo) is for the water intake and the carburettor filter is for old petrol engines.

f1638cea2877.exp: Fire buckets serve for fighting fires and, if necessary, for bailing water. They are not used for transferring fuel, because they would be contaminated, and they are not a substitute for extinguishers but a complement.

16f0d113c3bd.exp: If the engine is cooled with sea water, you must check that the seacock (válvula de fondo, grifo de fondo) is open, which lets outside water into the cooling circuit. If it were closed, the engine would overheat and be damaged. The thermostat regulates the temperature of the internal coolant.

fec3fd2d918b.exp: The Boutakow curve is a manoeuvre for approaching a person in the water when they are in sight: the helm is put to the side of the fall, a turn of about 60 degrees is made, then the helm is changed to the opposite side until reaching the reciprocal course and you advance. It is not a heaving-to (capeo) manoeuvre, nor a search without visibility, nor a berthing manoeuvre.

e375cacce980.exp: Running before the storm (correr el temporal) is putting the stern to the sea and sailing with the wind and waves astern until it abates. Heaving to (capear) is putting the bow to the sea, lying a-hull (pairear) is leaving the boat almost stopped, and 'sotaventear' is used in another context. Mnemonic: correr = flee with the stern to the sea.

d5f043e40e58.exp: Running before the storm (correr el temporal) consists of putting the stern to the sea and sailing with the waves astern until it abates. Putting the bow to the sea is heaving to (capear), and lying beam-on or on the bow is dangerous because the wave can capsize or flood the boat.

1fffd3475fb5.exp: In a towing alongside (remolque abarloado) the two boats go together, side by side, joined by lines. The port of one is joined to the starboard of the other. It is a permitted system, and the towing boat goes beside the towed one, not pushing nor ahead.

0bb0133254b2.exp: The radar reflector serves so that our boat is detected by the radar of other ships, since its metallic geometry returns the waves received. It does not indicate presence to others nor emit signals; nor is it a beacon or distress equipment.

db892a799f09.exp: The radar reflector is a passive device, with a metal surface, that returns the radar waves received from other ships, so that our boat shows up better on their screens. It does not emit or amplify signals, nor is it used to call for help.

94f05f04a069.exp: A person in the water is given hot non-alcoholic drinks (sugared water, tea, broth) to help them recover temperature. Alcohol dilates the blood vessels of the skin and increases heat loss, and stimulants overload the heart. Water with bicarbonate is not indicated.

55ec7b50fa69.exp: In an electrical storm the radio equipment and antennas are disconnected to protect the equipment from a discharge or from overvoltages induced by lightning. Lowering sails or moderating speed do not reduce the electrical risk, and the compass is not what matters; if anything, it should be protected from intense magnetic fields.

f6f655dd1eb0.exp: A shoal (bajo) is an area of little depth, normally with rocks or sand, which can be dangerous for the hull and the draught (calado) of the boat. That is why it is indicated on the chart and with beacons. It has nothing to do with freshwater springs, which do not alter the draught, nor with great depths.

337564bea14b.exp: With the towing alongside (remolque abarloado), tug and towed boat go joined side by side, and the tug is the one that provides the propulsion and main steering. The towed boat puts its helm somewhat towards the side opposite the tug to counteract the stern of the pair opening towards the tug's side. Here the tug is on the starboard side, so the helm goes somewhat to port.

a2d236f85c79.exp: Before leaving you must check everything: the weather forecast, the engine's fuel, oil and coolant, and the safety equipment (lifejackets, flares, rockets). Safe sailing depends on the sum of all those checks, so 'all are true' is the complete answer.

8f3241d0bcda.exp: The liferaft must be near the gunwale (borda), in a cradle that allows it to be launched quickly, and held by a lashing with a hydrostatic release (zafa hidrostática): if the boat sinks the release lets go at a few metres' depth and the raft rises and inflates. In a closed place, without securing or next to the engine it could not be used quickly or would be lost.

5104fadc8cac.exp: The radar reflector is a metal piece with flat faces that returns the echo of radar waves in the same direction they arrive from. This way the boat, which because it is small and made of fibreglass or wood would hardly be seen on the screen, appears as a clear echo on the radars of other ships. It emits nothing and sends no messages: it is passive, and only serves for us to be detected.

69859c5f6161.exp: The radar reflector is a metal piece with flat faces that returns the echo of radar waves in the same direction they arrive from. This way the boat, which because it is small and made of fibreglass or wood would hardly be seen on the screen, appears as a clear echo on the radars of other ships. It emits nothing and sends no messages: it is passive, and only serves for us to be detected.

4282f1e6f2b4.exp: The heliograph or signalling mirror (heliógrafo, espejo de señales) reflects sunlight and directs it with flashes towards a distant aircraft or ship, so it serves to attract attention and ask for help only when it is sunny. It is not for plotting courses or taking bearings (that is the alidade) and has nothing to do with medicine or repairing the raft.

f98d7ab374e5.exp: Parachute rockets and hand flares are used both by day and by night, whereas the orange smoke canister is only seen by day, because at night it cannot be distinguished. That is why the answer is the one that distributes the signals this way; the others limit to day only or night only signals that serve for both times.

7a277918d7b3.exp: The GPS M.O.B. (Man Over Board) function immediately stores, with a single key, the position of the point where the person fell and guides us back. Datum is the estimated search point, Go to directs to an already existing point and Distress is not a GPS function for this.

7d4c883650bf.exp: Rockets and flares are fired to leeward (sotavento, the side opposite the wind), so that the wind carries the sparks and incandescent debris away from the boat and the people. Firing to windward would make the ashes and smoke fall on the boat, with risk of burns or fire.

d6cb6d2cd9b5.exp: Stability (estabilidad) is the property of the ship of recovering its equilibrium position (upright, adrizado) when an external cause, such as wind or swell, has heeled it. It is not buoyancy (flotabilidad), which is staying afloat, nor manoeuvrability, which is the response to helm and engine. If the heel increased or persisted when the cause ceased, the boat would not be stable.

3310cbd94a7a.exp: In bad weather with the coast to leeward, the wind and waves push the boat towards land. You must gain windward, correcting the course towards the side the wind blows from, to move away from the coast and not be swept onto it. Correcting to leeward would bring us closer to danger.

4631de738944.exp: With the towing alongside (remolque abarloado), tug and towed boat go joined side by side, and the tug is the one that provides the propulsion and main steering. The towed boat puts its helm somewhat towards the side opposite the tug to counteract the stern of the pair opening towards the tug's side. Here the tug is on the port side, so the helm goes somewhat to starboard.

d9c576e9343e.exp: Putting the boat 'a son de mar' is leaving it prepared for bad weather: every object in its place, stowed and lashed, so that nothing rolls or bangs with the rolling and safety is compromised. It has nothing to do with bells, flags or cleaning the deck.

7a345f3e4bf6.exp: Towing alongside (remolque abarloado) is the kind done with the boats joined side by side, widely used in harbour manoeuvres. It is not prohibited by the COLREGs (RIPA); with the tug ahead it is a towing in line, and with the tug pushing astern it is not called abarloado.

a1b1e6e4ec29.exp: Cardiac massage (chest compressions) is done when there is cardiac arrest, that is, when the heart is not pumping blood. Haemorrhages are treated with compression or a tourniquet, and respiratory failure with ventilation; it is not the same as a stopped heart.

2593bbc9d996.exp: Salvamento Marítimo can be contacted by all means: VHF radio (channel 16 or digital selective calling on channel 70), mobile phone (900 202 202 or 112) and radio beacons (EPIRB). That is why the options saying exclusively or only one means are false: in an emergency any available means is valid, whichever works first and best.

03ac0acb0a59.exp: Salvamento Marítimo can be contacted by all means: VHF radio (channel 16 or digital selective calling on channel 70), mobile phone (900 202 202 or 112) and radio beacons (EPIRB). That is why the options saying exclusively or only one means are false: in an emergency any available means is valid, whichever works first and best.

4edc143e99ea.exp: Portable extinguishers must be in places of easy and quick access, visible and signposted, near the risk areas but not so close that they cannot be reached if there is a fire. Keeping them under lock or inside the engine compartment would make them impossible to use just when they are needed most.

f3753142ac2f.exp: The radar reflector is a metal piece with flat faces that returns the echo of radar waves in the same direction they arrive from. This way the boat, which because it is small and made of fibreglass or wood would hardly be seen on the screen, appears as a clear echo on the radars of other ships. It emits nothing and sends no messages: it is passive, and only serves for us to be detected.

1cb2204f33ca.exp: The GPS MOB (man overboard) function stores with a single button the exact position and time at which it is activated. With that point the GPS indicates course and distance to return to the place of the fall and organise the search or rescue. It does not plot the track nor make the boat visible to others. Datum is another concept: the estimated search point.

f1ca726b630d.exp: The mandatory lifejackets in navigation zones are sized by distance from the coast; the official key of this question bank gives 150 N for zone 4. It is a regulatory value worth memorising: the farther from the coast, the greater the buoyancy required (50 N, 100 N, 150 N, 275 N depending on the zone).
f1ca726b630d.duda: Possible error in the key: according to the safety equipment regulations, for zone 4 I recall 100 N (150 N would be zone 3); it is worth verifying.

6f577cd91bee.exp: Lying beam-on to the sea (atravesarse a la mar), that is, putting the side to the waves, makes transverse wave trains greatly increase the rolling (balance) and can end in capsize or shipping water. It must be avoided by changing course to take the sea on the bow or the quarter, and distributing weights helps, it is not what must be avoided.

96efa67dcab4.exp: The safety harness is not mandatory by regulation, but it is highly recommended, especially in bad weather, at night or when sailing alone, because it prevents falling into the water by securing you to the boat with a lifeline. That is why it neither states when nor how to use it, it only advises.

845b577c6e6a.exp: Loading weights near the keel lowers the boat's centre of gravity, and the lower it is relative to the metacentre, the greater the righting arm and the more stability. That is why ballast goes in the keel. Loading high weights produces the opposite: the centre of gravity rises and stability is reduced.

bf686e592497.exp: Pitching (cabeceo) is the longitudinal (bow-stern) oscillation of the boat due to the waves, like a seesaw. Rolling (balance), on the other hand, is the transverse oscillation (from port to starboard). Mnemonic: head up and down = cabeceo; side to side = balance.

e1623d234f57.exp: Rolling (balance) is the alternating inclination of the boat towards one side and the other due to the action of the sea. Pitching (cabezada, cabeceo) is the movement from bow to stern. 'Vaivén' and period do not designate this movement: the period is the time of one complete oscillation.

d381900a5b98.exp: The expanding square search (exploración en espiral cuadrada) is used when the person in the water cannot be seen: you sail around the datum describing a growing square, with a spacing S between tracks that is increased on each turn. The sector search (exploración por sectores) is done as a star passing through the datum, and the circular one in concentric circles; Boutakow and Anderson are manoeuvres with the person in the water in sight.

1b6f8b7f0959.exp: The Boutakow curve is a manoeuvre for approaching a person in the water when they are in sight: the helm is put to the side of the fall until we have turned about 60 degrees from the initial course, then it is changed to the opposite side to return along our wake and approach the person in the water from windward. It is not for heaving to (capear), nor for berthing, nor for searching for someone who cannot be seen.

6f111dbdb00f.exp: Stability (estabilidad) is the property of the ship of recovering its equilibrium position (upright, adrizado) when an external cause, such as wind or swell, has heeled it. It is not buoyancy (flotabilidad), which is staying afloat, nor manoeuvrability, which is the response to helm and engine. If the heel increased or persisted when the cause ceased, the boat would not be stable.

3d214480935f.exp: In bad weather the seacocks must be closed to prevent water entering the hull through a broken pipe or because of the swell, but the engine cooling one must stay open, because the inboard engine is cooled with sea water and without it would overheat and stop just when we need it most.

b0022d5d0c37.exp: When the tug changes course, the towed boat must put its helm to the opposite side to the one the tug turns to. This avoids the 'estrechonazo', the sudden jerk produced when the towed boat, through inertia, veers towards the inside of the curve and shortens the line. Keeping the opposite side keeps the line taut and the towed boat in the wake.

9f7c8e8f1774.exp: Heaving to in the storm (capear el temporal) is taking the sea on the bow (bow opened about 30-40 degrees to the wave) at low speed, just enough to keep steerage. This way the boat climbs the waves gently and avoids the heavy rolling of the beam sea and the danger of a following sea. Running before the storm (correr el temporal), on the other hand, is taking the sea on the stern or quarter.

1799d2829508.exp: Heaving to in the storm (capear el temporal) is taking the sea on the bow (bow opened about 30-40 degrees to the wave) at low speed, just enough to keep steerage. This way the boat climbs the waves gently and avoids the heavy rolling of the beam sea and the danger of a following sea. Running before the storm (correr el temporal), on the other hand, is taking the sea on the stern or quarter.

a5730ad3ce2a.exp: The heliograph or signalling mirror (heliógrafo, espejo de señales) reflects sunlight and directs it with flashes towards a distant aircraft or ship, so it serves to attract attention and ask for help only when it is sunny. It is not for plotting courses or taking bearings (that is the alidade) and has nothing to do with medicine or repairing the raft.

2fe83c67a2c0.exp: The Boutakow curve is a manoeuvre for approaching a person in the water when they are in sight: the helm is put to the side of the fall until we have turned about 60 degrees from the initial course, then it is changed to the opposite side to return along our wake and approach the person in the water from windward. It is not for heaving to (capear), nor for berthing, nor for searching for someone who cannot be seen.

c724dc3a91ce.exp: The signalling mirror is also called a heliograph (heliógrafo) (helio = sun, grafo = write): it writes messages with flashes of sunlight. The heliometer is a different astronomical instrument, the radar reflector serves for radar and the alidade is the ring for taking bearings on a compass.

196031e64aee.exp: If we see the crew member fall, the rescue manoeuvre is the Anderson curve (or Williamson or Boutakow depending on the situation), which brings us back to the person in the water while still in sight. The searches (expanding square, sectors, circular) are for when the person in the water has been lost from sight and you have to search around the datum.

3bb9fce47da2.exp: The expanding square search (exploración en espiral cuadrada) is used when the person in the water cannot be seen: you sail around the datum describing a growing square, with a spacing S between tracks that is increased on each turn. The sector search (exploración por sectores) is done as a star passing through the datum, and the circular one in concentric circles; Boutakow and Anderson are manoeuvres with the person in the water in sight.

13600f298959.exp: The GPS M.O.B. (Man Over Board) function immediately stores, with a single key, the position of the point where the person fell and guides us back. Datum is the estimated search point, Go to directs to an already existing point and Distress is not a GPS function for this.

fce947dfd126.exp: In cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) chest compressions are done at a rate of 100 to 120 per minute, roughly the beat of a fast song, with a depth of about 5-6 cm. A rate of 60 or less is insufficient to maintain circulation; 8-10 per minute would be useless.

4ec1f7a377a0.exp: The radar reflector reflects waves that strike it in the same direction they arrived from, making our boat give a visible echo on other radars. It does not amplify them (it is a passive element without electronics), nor does it pick up signals from other ships, nor does it have anything to do with static electricity.

48c81a0d22cd.exp: The safety harness, attached to a lifeline, serves to prevent the crew member from falling into the water, especially in bad weather. It gives no buoyancy (that is what the lifejacket does) and it is not intended to release the crew member on falling: it holds them on the boat.

593401a9d045.exp: In reduced visibility (fog, rain, mist) the COLREGs (RIPA) require keeping a strict lookout, having the engine ready, reducing to a safe speed and making sound signals. These are the typical measures of navigation in restricted visibility, different from berthing, racing or navigating on rivers.

078fc2c33ed5.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras) are those whose depth is less than half the wavelength of the wave: then the bottom influences the wave, which slows down, becomes steeper and can break. With a depth greater than that half, the bottom does not interfere with the movement of the swell.

6ebd27b664a2.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras) are waters of little depth, that is, with the bottom close to the surface relative to the draught and the wave. The main risk is grounding (varada), so extreme precautions are taken: consult the chart for rocky bottoms or shoals, watch the sounder and have the anchor ready.

7283349df103.exp: When someone falls into the water with the boat under way, the helm is put to the side of the person's fall so that the stern and the propeller move away from them. This way the hull turns, moving the propeller away from the person in the water, who stays to one side. Putting it to the opposite side would take the stern and the propeller towards the crew member.

a64c437720b8.exp: If the boat is rolling dangerously beam-on to the sea, you must change course to take the waves on the bow or the quarter and reduce the rolling. Staying on course keeps the danger, and increasing or decreasing speed does not change the angle of the waves relative to the hull.

5e4589b5d184.exp: Before leaving you must check everything: the weather forecast, the engine's fuel, oil and coolant, and the safety equipment (lifejackets, flares, rockets). Safe sailing depends on the sum of all those checks, so 'all are true' is the complete answer.

08b992c87213.exp: Before leaving you must check everything: the weather forecast, the engine's fuel, oil and coolant, and the safety equipment (lifejackets, flares, rockets). Safe sailing depends on the sum of all those checks, so 'all are true' is the complete answer.

d2a99295772e.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras) are waters of little depth, that is, with the bottom close to the surface relative to the draught and the wave. The main risk is grounding (varada), so extreme precautions are taken: consult the chart for rocky bottoms or shoals, watch the sounder and have the anchor ready.

a04434d1c0d0.exp: So that the other ship realises we are manoeuvring, the COLREGs (RIPA) require course alterations to be large, clear and made in good time. At night, with lights, a small change is not distinguishable and could cause confusion. Whenever there is room, the manoeuvre must be broad and decisive.

47675f143940.exp: Cardiac massage is done with the patient face up on a hard surface, so that the compression of the chest squeezes the heart against the spine and pumps blood. A soft mattress would absorb the compression and make it ineffective; face down the sternum cannot be reached.

3e4be37258ad.exp: To reduce rolling (balance) the course is changed, avoiding taking the sea on the beam and putting it on the bow or the quarter. Lying beam-on increases it, the helm amidships does not change the angle relative to the waves, and moving weights does not solve the cause.

381c8aaa6f7e.exp: In an electrical storm the prudent thing is to disconnect or ground antennas and cables to prevent lightning from damaging the equipment, and to protect the compass with a metal box (Faraday cage). Switching on devices or keeping radar and GPS active exposes them, and directing the discharge to the engine is dangerous.

7f8c18ffd0d3.exp: A seacock (grifo de fondo) is a ball valve: it is closed when the handle is perpendicular (crosswise) to the direction of the pipe, and open when it is parallel, aligned with it. Mnemonic: parallel = water passes; crosswise = cut off. Seacocks do have a handle and can be open.

ab72a9a55b63.exp: A seacock (grifo de fondo) is a ball valve: it is closed when the handle is perpendicular (crosswise) to the direction of the pipe, and open when it is parallel, aligned with it. Mnemonic: parallel = water passes; crosswise = cut off. Seacocks do have a handle and can be open.

cffd6f6dc4a3.exp: The manoeuvre in the drawing, with a quick turn towards the side of the fall and then an opposite turn to return along the boat's own course towards the person in the water in sight, is the Anderson manoeuvre. Williamson makes a loop-shaped turn of 60 degrees and Scharnow is a different turning manoeuvre. Anderson is done with the person in the water in sight.

33a20aacfbf6.exp: The figure corresponds to the Boutakow curve: a manoeuvre for approaching a person in the water who is in sight. The expanding square, sector or circular searches are search manoeuvres when the person in the water cannot be seen and they trace patterns with spacing between tracks.

bca9bce6ed7f.exp: The expanding square search (exploración en espiral cuadrada) is used when the person in the water cannot be seen: you sail around the datum describing a growing square, with a spacing S between tracks that is increased on each turn. 968d09eaa2ce.exp: Running before the storm (correr el temporal) consists of taking the sea on the stern or quarter and letting yourself be carried along with it until it abates. It is different from heaving to (capear), which is taking the sea on the bow with little engine. Mnemonic: correr = flee with the storm behind; capear = face it head-on with the bow.

6185ce57a647.exp: The property is called stability (estabilidad): the ability to return to equilibrium after being heeled by wind or waves. Buoyancy (flotabilidad) is staying afloat, seaworthiness (navegabilidad) is the set of conditions for sailing safely. Heeling (escorar) is the inclination itself, not a property.

Keeping the opposite side keeps the line taut and the towed boat in the wake.

5aac2541553f.exp: Whenever possible, in bad weather it is best to sail with the sea on the bow or the quarter: rolling, pitching and the blows of the sea are better controlled. From ahead the hull is heavily punished, from astern there can be shipping of water or loss of steering, and on the beam the rolling is dangerous.

0eefbd5c40dd.exp: The towline must have a length such that tug and towed boat are in the same relative position on the wave, both in the trough or both on the crest. This way the line works steadily and without jerks. If one were on the crest and the other in the trough, the line would tighten and slacken abruptly.

2c6d7f88c491.exp: In an emergency Salvamento Marítimo is contacted by VHF radio channel 16 or by DSC on channel 70, and by telephone 900 202 202 or 112. The key accepts only the radio option; the telephone 803 020 020 is not that of Salvamento and letter or e-mail are not urgent means.
2c6d7f88c491.duda: Option a says Channel 16 UHF when it is VHF, and 112 and 900 202 202 are also valid, so the question is imprecise.

fe6323a71a64.exp: Salvamento Marítimo can be reached by the three means: telephone at 900 202 202, VHF channel 16 (or digital selective calling on channel 70) and also 112. All the options are valid, so 'all are correct'.

a1bb2f46c0e8.exp: In a tow, the one responsible for the passage plan (derrota, the route to follow) is the tug, which is the one with the propulsion and the overall view. The towed boat only obeys orders and steers as instructed. Neither the pilot nor the insurer makes that decision.

2d3895ca6d82.exp: The liferaft must be stowed near the gunwale (borda) and held by a lashing with a hydrostatic release (zafa hidrostática), so that, if the boat sinks, it releases itself and rises floating and inflating. It must be possible to launch it quickly, not stored in a closed place or near the engine.

b09100397255.exp: To heave to in the storm (capear), the sea is taken on the bow, at low speed. With the beam sea the rolling is dangerous, and with the quarter or the stern we would be running before the storm, not heaving to.

73c35070aefa.exp: Safety messages for navigation, such as weather warnings, are announced first on VHF channel 16, the distress, safety and calling channel, and then the working channel on which the text will be broadcast is indicated. Channel 70 is only for digital selective calling and not for voice.

30395e62380e.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras) are waters of little depth, that is, with the bottom close to the surface relative to the draught and the wave. The main risk is grounding (varada), so extreme precautions are taken: consult the chart for rocky bottoms or shoals, watch the sounder and have the anchor ready.

077202ac3b63.exp: Flares and rockets are fired to leeward (sotavento) so that the wind carries the sparks and smoke away from the boat and its occupants. If it were done to windward, the incandescent debris would fall on the boat or the people, with risk of burns or fire.

d0c4ee8fd13f.exp: The parachute rocket, which climbs high and is seen from a great distance, is used when a ship on the horizon or an aircraft is sighted, so that they see us. It is not a signal for the moment of abandoning ship nor is it only for daytime: it serves by day and by night.

828806869631.exp: In thick fog the regulation sound signals set by the COLREGs (RIPA) for reduced visibility are made (blasts at two-minute intervals depending on the type of vessel). Frequent changes of course or stops do not warn other ships and can create confusion.

08c780efc4cc.exp: The regulation lifebuoys for zone 4 carry an automatically activated light, to locate them at night, and a line (rabiza, floating rope) so the person in the water can be grasped and recovered. The radar reflector is not a complement to the lifebuoy.

309e969cc15f.exp: The instrument that uses sunlight to attract attention and ask for help is the signalling mirror or heliograph (heliógrafo). The heliometer and the alidade are other instruments, and the radar reflector only returns radar waves. As it depends on the sun, it can only be used by day.

7c7a98848e93.exp: The heliograph (heliógrafo) is the signalling mirror that reflects sunlight in flashes to attract attention and ask for help. The alidade is used to take bearings, the radar reflector to be detected by radar, and solar panels generate electricity, not flashes.

dbf9e8e9fd09.exp: If we see the crew member fall, the rescue manoeuvre is the Anderson curve (or Williamson or Boutakow depending on the situation), which brings us back to the person in the water while still in sight. The searches (expanding square, sectors, circular) are for when the person in the water has been lost from sight and you have to search around the datum.

9657db02b26c.exp: The expanding square search (exploración en espiral cuadrada) is used when the person in the water cannot be seen: you sail around the datum describing a growing square, with a spacing S between tracks that is increased on each turn. The sector search (exploración por sectores) is done as a star passing through the datum, and the circular one in concentric circles; Boutakow and Anderson are manoeuvres with the person in the water in sight.

c5a18cf02a48.exp: Fire buckets are multipurpose equipment: they serve to put out fires with water (above all of solid materials) and, if necessary, to bail water out of the boat. They are not used to transfer fuel, which is dangerous and absurd, and they are not limited to putting out fires nor replaced by extinguishers, which are a complement.

761ac36529d9.exp: Synchronism (sincronismo) occurs when the period of the waves coincides with the boat's rolling or pitching period, and the movements are amplified. It is broken by changing course (or speed), which changes the period at which the boat meets the waves. Shifting or throwing weights is not a suitable manoeuvre and increasing speed can make it worse.

863b7cdfece3.exp: Transverse synchronism (rolling) occurs when the boat's rolling period coincides with that of the waves. To break it you must alter the period at which the waves reach the hull, and the most effective thing is to change course. Shifting weights to one side only heels the boat without solving the problem.

e5b8d081f08f.exp: In an electrical storm there is a risk that lightning or overvoltages will damage the electronic and radio equipment. That is why the radio equipment (and its antennas) is disconnected and touching connected metal parts is avoided. Lowering sails or moderating speed does not protect from lightning, and the nautical compass has nothing to do with the matter.

1feafe2d8ea2.exp: Heaving to (capear) is riding out the storm without making much headway: the bow (or the bow quarter) is put to the sea and minimum speed is maintained, just enough to steer. This way the boat rides the waves without taking them on the side, where it could capsize or ship water. Going at full power strains the hull and taking the waves beam-on is dangerous.

e4a42df6b272.exp: The radar reflector is a passive device, made of metal sheets, that reflects the waves it receives back towards the emitter and so makes the boat appear better on the screen of other radars. It neither amplifies nor emits anything and does not pick up signals. It is especially useful on small fibreglass or wooden boats, which reflect little.

8869ac39796e.exp: Correctly stowed inflatable rafts are already designed to release only when the boat sinks, thanks to the hydrostatic release (zafa hidrostática), which cuts the lashing at a few metres' depth, not through a blow from the sea. Reinforcing the release or the lashings would prevent it from being freed when needed. Therefore, they are left as they are.

a6acfeff78fe.exp: Shallow waters (aguas someras, or of little depth) are those in which the depth is less than half the wavelength of the wave. In them the bottom slows the wave, which becomes shorter, higher and steeper and can break. In deep water the depth exceeds half the wavelength and the bottom has no influence.

258a8f93583f.exp: If the crew member falls over the port side, the rudder blade is put to that same side, that is, to port. This way the stern swings to the opposite side and the propeller moves away from the person in the water. Putting the tiller to the opposite side (starboard) would take the stern towards the person and the propeller could injure them.

83c8a9080a9e.exp: The maximum speed inside ports is 3 knots, to avoid waves that damage moored boats and for the safety of manoeuvres and people. It is a general rule of port regulations; 3 knots is remembered as the walking speed in port.

7c7768e24fbe.exp: According to MARPOL, the discharge of hydrocarbons and oily mixtures from a pleasure craft is prohibited in any case. The distances of 3, 12 or 24 miles and the prior treatments apply to other waste (garbage, sewage), not to oil or fuel. Oily waste is handed in at port.

2bf9c66086a0.exp: If the beach is not buoyed, it may be approached but with caution: speed not exceeding 3 knots and avoiding endangering human life, as there may be swimmers, divers or canoeists. It is not freely accessible at any speed, and sound or light signals do not replace prudence or reduced speed.

75fb1b69cce3.exp: The MARPOL Convention (Annex IV) calls sewage (aguas sucias) the water from toilets, urinals and sick bays, which are the ones containing human waste. They differ from grey water (aguas grises: washbasins, showers, galley), which is not sewage in the strict sense. Black water (aguas negras) is the colloquial expression, but the convention's term is aguas sucias.

732478891762.exp: Food waste that has not been comminuted can only be discharged 12 miles or more from the coast outside special areas. If it is comminuted (particles smaller than 25 mm), 3 miles is enough. Even if it is organic, the minimum distance depends on the prior treatment; it can never be thrown anywhere.

c2c86ef09f9a.exp: Sewage (aguas sucias) can be discharged from 3 miles if the ship has approved equipment to comminute and disinfect it, and sails at least at 4 knots, with gradual discharge. Without that equipment, the minimum distance rises to 12 miles. Speed only permits the discharge provided the distance is also met.

547069372375.exp: In the MARPOL terminology used in the questionnaire, the water from washbasins, toilets and sick bays is grouped as sewage (aguas sucias). Black water (aguas negras) and wastewater (aguas residuales) are colloquial or generic expressions, and polluting water (aguas contaminantes) is not a term of the convention. It is the same designation as that of the toilet.

f5a77c1ecf9d.exp: Rendering assistance is a legal and moral obligation: the skipper must help anyone who asks for it at sea if they can do so without serious danger, and if they cannot, must report it to someone who can (Salvamento Marítimo, other ships). It does not depend on the navigation zone, the type of boat or the means available. The associated figure has no relation to the question.

75b3f9d2cdc9.exp: On beaches there is a strip of 200 metres from the shore reserved exclusively for swimmers, where navigation and anchoring are prohibited. Outside it, in the rest of the coast, a clearance of 50 metres is kept in areas of cliffs or isolated swimmers. Remember: 200 m for beaches.

b5a981edcc8e.exp: At the harbour mouth, ships leaving have right of way over those entering, because the one leaving has worse visibility and less room to manoeuvre, and the one entering can wait outside. It is a common safety rule in port regulations. The side (port or starboard) of the one entering does not change the rule.

c5981c63793f.exp: The SOLAS Convention (Safety of Life at Sea), in its chapter V, regulation 33, obliges every master to render assistance to persons in distress. MARPOL deals with pollution, ZEPIM is an environmental protection designation, and IMO is the organisation that promotes the conventions, not a convention itself.

730c6accfbb1.exp: ZEPIM stands for Specially Protected Area of Mediterranean Importance (Zona Especialmente Protegida de Importancia para el Mediterráneo) and is created under the Barcelona Convention to protect biodiversity. In Catalonia they are the Medes Islands and Cap de Creus. Zeppelin, MARPOL and PIME do not designate marine protection zones.

1ea9c6fe21d3.exp: Posidonia oceanica is a marine plant that forms meadows fundamental in the Mediterranean: they produce a lot of oxygen, shelter numerous species and protect beaches from erosion. When anchoring, the anchor and chain tear out the clumps, which take centuries to recover. They are not bathing zones, fishing zones or zones where navigation is prohibited.

4c5b7c0bc0dc.exp: Regulation 2 of MARPOL Annex V (garbage) establishes that its provisions apply to all ships, regardless of type, size or use, including pleasure craft. It is not limited to merchant ships nor to ships carrying dangerous goods nor to a specific area.

6644935a4afb.exp: The flag in the drawing is red with a white diagonal stripe: it is the modified Bravo, which indicates a diver in the water. It is not the Bravo of the International Code (red with a swallowtail cut, dangerous goods), nor the Alfa (white and blue), nor Hotel nor Charlie. Remember: red with a white diagonal is the diving flag.

224e3446453c.exp: Boats must keep a safety distance of 50 metres from the diving area, which is marked with a buoy with an Alfa or modified Bravo flag. Only the divers' support boat may approach. 75, 100 or 150 metres do not apply.

700ed6a89c1f.exp: Near cliffs (within 50 metres) there is a risk of rockfalls and the presence of swimmers or divers, so speed is limited to 3 knots. The generic safe speed is not enough and 5 knots or 25 km/h do not correspond to the rule. Remember: 50 metres, 3 knots.

bccd3e63a92d.exp: The flag in the drawing is white (hoist side) and blue with a swallowtail cut: it is the Alfa of the International Code of Signals, which indicates diver down, keep clear and proceed slowly. Hotel is half white half red vertically, November is white and blue checks and Bravo is red with a swallowtail cut.

824a698d0037.exp: The modified Bravo flag, red with a white diagonal stripe, is the signal that indicates a diver in the water, unlike the original Bravo (dangerous goods), which is red with a swallowtail cut. It is used on buoys or support boats, and requires keeping a distance. Man overboard or fishing gear are other signals.

41f9f346d27c.exp: A buoy with a red flag and a white diagonal stripe is the modified Bravo flag, which marks the presence of a diver in the water. It must not be confused with the Bravo flag of the international code (dangerous goods), which is all red with a swallowtail cut. A distance of 50 metres must be kept.

465b22109a96.exp: Cooking oil is a polluting waste and not food waste, so it cannot be thrown into the sea at any distance, neither filtered nor treated. It must be handed in at port. The distances of 3 and 12 miles apply to food scraps, not to oils or fats.

747fbf5fe88f.exp: Plastics, including bags, are totally prohibited from being thrown into the sea in any circumstance under MARPOL Annex V. There are no distances or treatments that permit it. They are kept on board and handed in at port in the appropriate containers.

80ad5115a241.exp: With approved equipment to comminute and disinfect sewage, discharge is permitted from 3 miles from the nearest land, sailing at least at 4 knots and with a moderate discharge rate. Without equipment, the distance is 12 miles. Speed alone never permits discharging at any distance.

f49292570514.exp: Without approved equipment to comminute and disinfect sewage, it is prohibited to discharge less than 12 miles from the coast. With equipment, the limit drops to 3 miles. Remember: 3 miles with equipment, 12 without it; in both cases with a minimum speed of 4 knots.

52de5ae99d86.exp: To discharge sewage under the authorised conditions you must sail at a minimum speed of 4 knots, so that the discharge disperses. To that speed are added the minimum distance from the coast and the condition of having equipment, if discharging between 3 and 12 miles. With less speed it cannot be discharged.

28b8f944b2a9.exp: Anchoring on Posidonia oceanica is an offence because it damages this protected plant. The authority's agents can report the skipper and oblige them to weigh anchor and move to another anchorage. That the sea is free does not exempt from respecting environmental protection rules.

2ead69c3ccd2.exp: In the event of an oil spill, Salvamento Marítimo must be notified (on 900 202 202 or VHF channel 16), which coordinates the response to marine pollution. Fire brigade, local police, town council or yacht club are not the competent bodies to coordinate the fight against pollution at sea.

b16ccb1c8816.exp: The MARPOL Convention regulates the prevention of pollution from ships, including garbage (Annex V), hydrocarbons and sewage. SOLAS deals with safety of life, ZEPIM with protected areas and IMO is the international organisation that adopts the conventions.

ff66babd33a2.exp: Between 3 and 12 miles, sewage can only be discharged if the ship has equipment to comminute and disinfect it, and sails at least at 4 knots. If not, you must move more than 12 miles away. That is why the key condition is having that equipment, not the season of the year nor a speed of 3 knots.

0b4fe536c621.exp: The telephone number of Salvamento Marítimo for reporting an oil spill or other maritime emergency is 900 202 202 (free). There is also 112 and VHF channel 16. Remember that 900 202 202 repeats the 2-0-2 pattern.

8112c699d381.exp: On entering and leaving port, boats leaving the harbour mouth have priority, since they have less visibility and manoeuvrability and the one entering can wait. It is a safety rule in ports that must be respected; it does not depend on the side from which one comes.
